correctness.rationale: For every m>=3 the Ramos all-vertices-sink two-particle cubical retraction removes precisely the interiors of m diagonal squares from C_m x C_m, a cellulated torus. Their open interiors are disjoint (though square boundaries meet at corners); taking m small disjoint invariant inner disks and retracting the intervening annuli onto the square boundaries gives a genus-one orientable surface with m boundary components, homotopy equivalent to K_m and thus wedge of m+1 circles. The transposition fixes exactly the m diagonal vertices and no oriented one- or allowed two-cells, giving Lefschetz number m, H1 trace 1-m, eigen-dimensions (+, -)=(1,m). This is an all-m topological proof, not an inference from the saved mod-p tests.

Finite modular checks m=3..12 cannot certify all m; the punctured-torus argument does.

originality.rationale: Prior cactus-graph general theorem DOES ALREADY CONTAIN the cycle integral Betti ranks and exact label-swap H1 character after E=m,b=1; these are NOT original in isolation. However that published theorem explicitly restricts itself to homology and disclaims a homotopy classification: H1 and H2 ranks, even with group action, do not imply a free fundamental group or wedge-of-circles homotopy. The present central explicit all-m homotopy equivalence and free fundamental group remain distinguishable in inspected statements. This is narrow best-of-knowledge novelty, not priority asserted for the already-covered representation.
residual_risks: Two of the three displayed conclusions (rank and transposition character) are covered by a stronger published cactus theorem and should never be promoted as independent discoveries.
The sole remaining homotopy classification is an elementary punctured-surface deduction from a preexisting cubical model; a reader may view it as a routine corollary despite its natural pi1 content.

value.rationale: The natural simplest non-tree sink graph family has an explicit complete space-level classification for every subdivision size m, giving free fundamental group of rank m+1 and supporting equivariant topological checks. That is strictly stronger information than the already published integral homology/character; the exact homotopy shape is a useful reusable benchmark for higher-particle or more-complicated sink graphs, even though the derivation is short. Value is assigned to that homotopy information alone, not to recomputing known ranks.
residual_risks: Very narrow homotopy specialization of an established model; significance is specific and does not amount to a new general theorem.
